doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Eddie Vinson and the Pacific Brass Band
title: Eddie Vinson's family and how he and Tom learned music together
summary: Tom tells how he and the trombonist Eddie Vinson, whose cousin and sister he married, learned together. The French professor stopped Vinson from coming to Nussie Rubin's lessons because Vinson was doing the learning. Vinson's father was a caulker and no one else in the family played.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: You mentioned a few minutes ago about Vinson, the trombone, Eddie Vinson, the trombone player. I never did get to see him or hear him. He died so long ago, I guess up in Chicago. Yeah, he died. Can you tell us any more about him, what he was like and anything, do you know anything about his family or folks, where he came from?
Yeah, I know his family. He came out of John's source, he raised up with him. Yeah, yeah. I married his cousin. You married his cousin?

Yeah, I married his cousin and we, we played together and his father, we was learning together, me and him. So he was playing routine and I learned him the music. Yeah. I learned him the music. He was playing routine and I learned him the music and so him and Nussie Rubin was playing, had a professor over here from the French opera. Where did you see that? No, right here. You know the French opera they had, yeah. Yeah, Rubin and Toulouse. Yeah, well he used to come over here and take lessons, Nussie Rubin, with his trombone. So Eddie used to come over with him and so the professor told him, he said don't bring that fellow over here no more. Because Nussie was paying, paying for the lesson and Eddie was testing it all. He was doing most of the lesson. Yeah. So Eddie took up the horn and he went, come on and made a couple of notes on the horn. He told him don't bring that fellow over here no more. He's a French fellow, right in the French quarters here. Yeah. So we learned together. We wear the same clothes. Yeah. He was a dad and I married his sister in the house, in his house. And where did he live about in Algeria? He lived in a place called Socks' Lane. John Socks' Lane.
Right behind the Naval Station. Right behind the Naval Station.
Yeah, that's what we learned right there. And me and him was together. We learned together, we played together for years. You say his father played something too or not?
No, his father was a caulker. His father was a caulker. Didn't play any? No, no, at all.
And we uh. Did he have any brothers or anybody else in the family that played music? No. Just Eddie.
No, just Eddie. Cause his sister, none of them didn't play no music. Just Eddie. We didn't just stay there and played on the ground. And we had a band.
